title: The 10 Best Tire Changers
subtitle: Manual, air-assisted, and shop tire changers for the home garage, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A tire changer pays for itself fast if you swap your own tires, run a trailer, or keep a second set of wheels. Amazon's range runs from $60 manual stands for wheels up to 16 inches, to air-assisted portable changers around $400, to 500-pound shop machines near $1,100 that handle 24-inch rims. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (bead breaker, powered operation, rim protection, and a bead blaster).

avoid.name: Krysolad Manual Tire Changer Machine, 8 to 21 in. Tire Change
avoid.flag: No bead breaker in the kit
avoid.verdict: It promises 8 to 21 inch wheels and quick bead breaking from a 23-pound duck-head kit, but the parts list doesn't include anything that breaks a bead. The TUFFIOM costs about $100 less and comes with a bead breaker.
reasons: The kit is listed as a duckbill adapter, a mounting base, and conical washers. There's no bead breaker, yet the same bullet says it "separates tire bead in seconds." Breaking the bead is the hardest part of a tire change.
It claims 8 to 21 inch fitment, but a buyer reports their 8 in. golf-cart tires wouldn't work on it at all.
It's pitched as "ideal for tabletop use" and as an upgrade for professional shops: a 23 lb stand on a 10 in. base isn't stable enough for either a 21 in. wheel or daily shop work.
The title says 8 to 21 inch "tire" while the bullets say 8 to 21 inch "rims", which are very different sizes.

buyers_guide.q: Will a manual tire changer handle my car's wheels?
buyers_guide.a: Check your rim size first. The classic manual stands here (TUFFIOM, VEVOR, Olympia) stop at 16 in., and EASYBERG and MOTOOS at 16.5 in. Most cars sold in the last decade ride on 17 in. or larger wheels, which need a changer rated to 21 in. or more, like the LCTX, the KATOOL KT-1030P, or a full shop machine.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need an air compressor?
buyers_guide.a: Manual stands don't. The LCTX, KATOOL KT-1030P, and both KATOOL shop machines use compressed air for the bead breaker or clamps, and the shop machines want 116 to 145 psi. A small pancake compressor won't keep up; plan on a tank of 20 gallons or more.

A bead blaster is a burst of air through a ring or nozzle that snaps a tire's bead onto the rim. Stiff run-flats, low-profile tires, and big off-road tires often won't seat with an ordinary air chuck. The KATOOL KT-T810 has one built in; for the others you can buy a separate bead seater tank.

buyers_guide.q: Will a tire changer scratch alloy wheels?
buyers_guide.a: A bare steel bar can. Look for a plastic or covered mount head and jaw covers. The KATOOL ME-T500 and KT-T810 include non-marring covers, and the Rabaconda uses a plastic mount head. With a manual stand, use rim protectors and plenty of tire lube.

buyers_guide.q: Can I balance tires with a tire changer?
buyers_guide.a: No. A changer only mounts and dismounts tires. You'll still need to balance the wheel afterward, either at a shop or with a wheel balancer. See our wheel balancer rankings for bubble and computerized options.
